brief.action.non_goal_flag: ⚠ Looks like it crosses a declared non-goal: {non_goal}
brief.attention.share: **{pct}%** of the last {days} days of model output went to **{project}** — effort, not importance
brief.automation.summary: Of {total} open: **{hook} hookable**, {skill} at the skill layer (one human step left), {explore} still exploratory, {unknown} unassessed; **{human_perm} need credentials or authorisation and will always be yours to do**.
brief.banner.backlog_full: ⚠ The backlog is at its hard ceiling of {max}. **Nothing new may be created today.** Run `{command}` and clear some out.
brief.banner.late: ⚠ This run is {hours}h later than its {slot} slot; activity windows were recomputed against the real time.
brief.banner.stale: ⚠ **This brief has not been updated in {days} days.**
brief.footer: *Generated by `{generator}` at {time}. Every claim here passed the evidence gate; whatever could not be verified was not rendered.*
brief.header.title: Daily brief · {date} ({weekday}) {time}
brief.next.decision: **Go get the evidence that answers it** (below)
brief.ordering.suppressed: **Not ranked today.** Most projects share the top importance band, so the order below would be decided by deadlines and recent activity rather than by what matters — say which of these outranks the others in `nextbrief review`.
brief.proposed.how: agree: `nextbrief done {id}` · disagree: `nextbrief ok {id}` clears the suggestion and leaves it open
brief.proposed.note: An agent thinks these are finished. It is not allowed to say so, only to suggest it -- so nothing happens until you answer.
brief.section.agent_queue: What an agent could do for you tonight
brief.section.decision_pending: Awaiting a decision (not procrastination — missing evidence)
brief.section.next_actions: Do these first (across the portfolio, not a few per project)
brief.section.stalled: Stalled (no next step) — the column GTD cares about most
brief.stalled.generic: **{name}** — {extra}Give it a concrete next step, or archive it on purpose.
brief.stalled.uncommitted: **{name}** — {count} uncommitted change(s) left sitting there. Either commit them and name a next step, or set its status to frozen so it stops showing up.
brief.stalled.uncommitted_dormant: **{name}** — parked, but {count} uncommitted change(s) are sitting in it. Commit them: work that exists only in a working tree of a repository nobody opens is the easiest kind to lose.
brief.truncated: ⚠ The brief ran past its {max}-line ceiling; {lines} lines were cut — whole sections, lowest-value first. The full data is in `{path}`; raise `caps.brief_max_lines` if this keeps happening.
brief.v0_note: *(v0: nothing has interpreted this yet, so what follows is deterministic fact only. Run `{command}` to get "what to do next".)*
brief.whatsnew.neglected: **{name}** has gone past its quiet limit
brief.whatsnew.none: Nothing has newly stalled or gone quiet since {at}.
cli.close.draft_hint: {accept} to take the draft  ·  Enter to skip  ·  or just write your own
cli.closed.footer: {n} closed item(s); {blank} with no record of what happened; {fw} piece(s) of future work, {open} still not turned into items.
cli.closed.how: nextbrief followup <id> turns those into backlog items.
cli.context.empty: No inventory yet — run `nextbrief sense` first.
cli.context.footer: {n} project(s); {absent} with no description. Add one to registry.jsonc as `description`, or to the project's own README.
cli.defer.needs_until: defer needs --until: a date (2026-09-01) or what you are waiting on ("after Fernwood ships"). A deferral that never comes back is a drop with better manners, so this one is not optional.
cli.defer.not_deferred: {id} is not deferred, so there is nothing to cancel.
cli.defer.past_date: note: {date} is in the past, so {id} is deferred and immediately due -- it stays in the brief.
cli.defer.until_condition: {id} -> deferred until: {when}. Nothing can watch for that, so it also comes back on {date} ({days} days) to be looked at again.
cli.defer.until_date: {id} -> deferred until {date}. It comes back into the brief that morning, on its own.
cli.describe.missing: Which project, and what is it? For example: nextbrief describe orchard "A tenancy API for multi-site retailers."
cli.describe.unknown: No project called {id}. Run `nextbrief projects` to see the ids.
cli.describe.where: Recorded in {path}. Your registry is untouched; a `description` typed there wins over this.
cli.do.hint: Enter for the first  ·  a number  ·  or type a path  ·  p to see the prompt  ·  q to cancel
cli.done.ask_future: Anything this turned up that does not belong to it? One per line, Enter on an empty line to finish.
cli.done.ask_summary: What actually happened? One line -- especially anything the item did not say. Enter to skip.
cli.done.cancelled: Cancelled. {id} was not closed and nothing was written.
cli.done.future_hint: {n} follow-up(s) recorded. `nextbrief followup {id}` turns them into backlog items, each carrying discovered_from: {id}.
cli.done.pick_ticks: Which of these are done? Up/down to move, space to toggle, Enter when finished.
cli.drop.done: {id} -> dropped (the file stays, and so does its git history)
cli.followup.about_to: About to create {n} backlog item(s) in {project}, each carrying discovered_from: {src}:
cli.followup.header: Future work recorded when {id} was closed:
cli.followup.how: nextbrief followup {id} --promote <n>  ·  --all for every one not already promoted.
cli.followup.not_a_number: {value} is not one of the numbers below.
cli.item.not_found: No item {id}. Run `nextbrief ls` to see what there is.
cli.ls.col.title: title
cli.ls.parked: {n} item(s) deferred and not due yet -- nextbrief ls --deferred
cli.ls.unconfirmed: {n} item(s) not confirmed yet (a '.' in the ok column). Confirming means: this is real, and written the way you meant it.
cli.ls.unconfirmed_how: nextbrief ok <id> to confirm  ·  drop <id> to reject  ·  show <id> to read it
cli.ok.done: {id} confirmed -- automatic decay will never touch it again.
cli.projects.empty: No snapshot yet — run `nextbrief sense` first.
cli.projects.head.name: name
cli.prune.how: Work through them with: nextbrief ok <id>  ·  done <id>  ·  drop <id>
cli.prune.no_snapshot: These match every other rule, but project evidence cannot be checked without state/snapshot.json. Run `nextbrief sense` and ask again.
cli.prune.rules: Decay rules: open for {days} days or more · created_by starts with '{prefix}' · never confirmed by you · the project has shown no evidence in the same window.
cli.prune.scope: Automatic decay only withdraws an agent's own unconfirmed proposals, and only when the project has shown no evidence at all for the whole window. Anything you wrote or confirmed is never dropped for you.
evidence.caveat_mtime: *file timestamps; no git in this repo*
html.adjust.title: This has not looked active for a while — say what it really is, and the next run will pick it up
html.banner.dropped: **Dropped {count} claim(s)** whose evidence would not check out; they are not shown. See `{path}`.
html.banner.late: This run is {hours}h later than its {slot} slot; activity windows were recomputed against the real time.
html.footer.evidence_gate: Every claim passed the evidence gate: anything whose source does not resolve in `snapshot.json` was never rendered.
html.footer.same_data: Generated by `{generator}` at {time}, from the same data as `BRIEF.md` — the two cannot drift apart.
html.header.title: Daily brief · {date} ({weekday})
html.next.decision: Go get the evidence that answers it
html.note.agent_queue: Open one to see what it can do and what is left for you. `{command}` opens a session in the right directory with the context already loaded.
html.note.decision_pending: This is not procrastination, it is a missing judgement. What follows is **the evidence that would settle it**.
html.note.next_actions: Ranked across the whole portfolio, not a few picked from each project.
html.note.proposed: An agent thinks these are finished. It may suggest it and nothing more, so they stay open until you answer.
html.note.unconfirmed: These were drafted **for you** out of your own project documents, and you have not signed off on them yet. Confirming (`{confirm}`) means "this is real, and it says what I meant" — after that, automatic decay never touches it. Leaving one unconfirmed loses nothing; it just sinks in the ranking over time. If it is wrong, `{drop}`.
html.section.agent_queue: What an agent could do for you tonight
